title: Is this a fair comparison?

claim: A and B are a fair pair (five months apart, 2.323 and 2.322 µm, no flags at the target), and Epsilon Indi B looks the same in both. A and C look different because C shows 4.94 µm light, where Epsilon Indi B stands out and most stars fade.
observations: In A a bright dot sits just below and right of the marker. With flagged pixels shown it is marked as a problem flag, so it is a bad pixel, not a change. In C most field stars fade while Epsilon Indi B stays bright.
uncertainty: No brightness was measured and each plate is stretched for display, so I cannot say whether Epsilon Indi B got brighter or fainter.
case_limitations: The quality screen checks for problem flags in a small circle around the predicted position. It is not a detection test or a brightness measurement.
A is from Data Release 1 and B is from Quick Release 3 (both pipeline version v27). Quick-release products may be reprocessed later.
Display images are resampled and contrast-stretched for viewing; they are not used to measure brightness.

The marker is a catalog prediction from SIMBAD/Gaia proper motion, not a position measured by Perigee. Annual parallax and the Ba/Bb orbit are not modeled; both are well under one pixel (parallax changes the predicted A-to-B shift by about 0.5 arcsec).
No visible change is not the same as no change: the shared stretch clips Epsilon Indi B to white in A and B, and no brightness was measured.
